title: The Preparation of Chicken Ex Ovo Embryos and Chorioallantoic Membrane Vessels as In Vivo Model for Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound Imaging and Microbubble-Mediated Drug Delivery Studies
protocol: Store freshly fertilized chicken eggs at 15 °C for up to one week.
Place the stored fertilized eggs vertically with the pointy side down into a 37 °C, humidified incubator.
Warm up a heating plate to 37 °C.
Place a metal egg holder on the heating plate.
Place a metal weighing boat holder on the heating plate.
Fill an Erlenmeyer flask with PBS and place it on the heating plate.
Fill a weighing boat with a 10 mm layer of ultrasound gel and place it in the prewarmed holder.
Transfer a 5-day old incubated fertilized egg to the prewarmed metal egg holder.
Keep the egg in the same orientation with the date on top.
Make a small indent at the very top of the egg where the date is written using the pointy back of tweezers.
Create a second indent around 2/3 down the side of the egg using the pointy back of tweezers.
Remove a small piece of eggshell from the indented area on top of the egg using larger tweezers.
Ensure that the air sac in the top of the eggshell contacts the outside air without penetrating too deep into the shell.
Use a light source to check the position of the air sac inside the egg.
Penetrate the shell through the second indent on the side 2/3 down the egg using a 5 mL syringe and 19 G needle.
Withdraw approximately 2 mL of egg white.
Ensure the needle is pointing downwards towards the bottom of the egg to prevent damage to the embryo and CAM.
Use tape to seal any punctures made during the procedure.
Close the top hole of the egg with a finger to prevent egg white leakage.
Remove excess egg white with tissue if it continues to leak.
Empty the syringe by transferring the egg white to the weighing boat.
Use large tweezers to enlarge the small opening on the top of the egg.
Look inside the egg through the top opening to locate the embryo and CAM.
Continue removing eggshell while ensuring maximum visibility of the embryo and CAM.
Avoid letting the edge of the shell opening go below the CAM level.
Prevent penetration of the inner membrane and formation of sharp edges.
Turn the egg 180° after creating the opening, placing it back in the holder with the opening facing down.
Wait for 1-2 minutes until the embryo floats up and becomes invisible from the bottom.
Ensure that only yolk is visible before proceeding to the next step.
If the embryo is still visible after 2 minutes, turn the egg clockwise for 1-2 minutes.
Remove the tape from the side opening.
Check if the inside of the egg bulges out of the bottom opening.
If the egg does not bulge, use the needle on the syringe to puncture the side opening again, pointing upwards.
Continue until the egg bulges out of the bottom opening.
Hold the bottom of the egg close to the weighing boat in the metal weighing boat holder.
Gently but quickly make a horizontal scratch in the membrane over the entire width of the opening using one of the sharp points of the small tweezer.
Gently drop the egg content into the weighing boat.
If the egg content does not come out, use the needle on the syringe to puncture the side opening again with the needle pointing upwards.
If the embryo is in the weighing boat sideways, it will usually go up by itself.
If this does not happen, use a piece of tissue paper to reposition the embryo.
Put one side of the tissue paper on the embryo, drag the tissue paper to the other end, and release the tissue paper with a few drops of ~30 µL of PBS (37 °C) using a plastic Pasteur pipet.
Visually check the embryo for heartbeat and intact CAM vessels.
Discard the embryo if there is no heartbeat, bleeding, or yolk leakage.
Maintain the embryo and CAM at 37°C to prevent drying out.
Place small drops of ~30 μL of 37°C PBS on the embryo and CAM regularly.
Take out the needle and use tape to seal the gap on the side of the syringe.
Empty the syringe by adding egg white to the ultrasound gel in the weighing boat.
Use large tweezers to enlarge the small opening on the top of the egg.
Fill a syringe with ~1 mL more of 37 °C PBS than the withdrawn volume during step 1.3.2.4.
Take off the tape from the side gap, penetrate the gap with the filled syringe, and empty it into the shell.
Turn the egg 180° and place it back in the egg holder such that the opening faces towards the bottom.
Turn the egg clockwise until only yolk is visible.
Warm up a heating plate to 37 °C.
Place a metal weighing boat holder on the heating plate.
Place a 10 mL Erlenmeyer filled with PBS on the heating plate.
Fill a shallow container with 1 L of 37 °C PBS.
Place a weighing boat in a 90 mm diameter Petri dish.
Submerge the Petri dish and weighing boat completely in the container.
Take an 8-day old incubated egg from the incubator two hours before the experiment.
Rotate the egg 180° inside the incubator so that the top of the egg faces the bottom.
Wait for 1 hour, then rotate the egg back to its original position and leave it for another hour.
Hold an 8-day old incubated egg horizontally.
Make a small indent 1/2 down the egg using the pointy back of large tweezers.
Continue making small indents in a ring pattern around the eggshell at intervals of ~10 mm.
Create one bigger hole by cracking the shell between two small indents using the pointy back of large tweezers.
Submerge the egg in 37 °C PBS.
Keep the egg submerged for 5 minutes.
Gently open the egg along the small indents using thumbs.
Separate the two eggshell pieces by gently moving them back and forth.
Drop the egg content into the weighing boat.
Remove excess PBS from the weighing boat by slightly tilting it.
Pull glass needles from glass capillary tubes using a micro forge.
Break off a small part of the tip of the needle if it is not beveled.
Fill the glass needle with mineral oil and place it in a micro-injection system.
Ensure there are no air bubbles in the mineral oil in the glass needle.
Empty the pulled-glass capillary needle as far as the micro-injection system allows.
Partly refill the glass needle with air.
Put 10 µL of the desired solution on a piece of waxy film.
Leave the microbubble drop on the waxy film for ~1 min to concentrate the microbubbles.
Fill the glass needle with the microbubble solution by positioning the needle tip into the drop on the waxy film.
Aspirate the microbubble enriched solution from the top of the liquid drop.
Raise the tip of the glass needle to its highest point and wait for approximately 2 minutes before injecting.
Under a stereo microscope, select a vein on the CAM for injection.
Inject into one of the veins of the embryo using the prepared glass needle.
Choose an injection site that is a branch of the vessel to limit blood flow obstruction.
Position the glass needle parallel to the selected vein in the same focal plane as the vessel wall.
Ensure the needle tip touches the vessel wall.
Slowly advance the glass needle to penetrate the vessel wall.
Retract the needle slightly if it pierces through the entire vessel and reposition inside the lumen.
Lift the needle slightly after penetration to move forward along the vessel for better positioning.
Inject a small amount of solution to confirm correct position within the vessel lumen.
Ensure injected solution follows blood flow; adjust needle position by moving sideways if necessary.
Continue injecting small amounts until proper injection is confirmed.
Leave the glass needle in the vessel for approximately 15 seconds to prevent massive bleeding.
Move the glass needle sideways, up and down, and back and forth a few times to allow gentle retraction of the glass needle.
Use a new glass needle for each injection.
Take a cell culture chamber with two parallel 50 µm thick acoustically transparent polycarbonate membranes.
Remove one membrane from the holder using a scalpel along the glue line without damaging the other membrane.
Prepare approximately 15 mL of 2% agarose in demi-water solution by heating to between 80-95 °C.
Cool the glass beaker with the dissolved agarose solution under cold running water.
Slowly pour the solution into the holder with acoustic membrane until it fills up the entire holder.
Tilt the holder slightly so that the agarose layer distributes evenly inside the plastic frame.
Ensure the agarose layer is flat and let the agarose set at room temperature.
Take out the egg content from the egg as described in section 1.2, 1.3, or 1.4.
If needed, inject the CAM with microbubbles and/or other solutions as described in section 2.1.2.
Fill a 1 L Petri dish with approximately 500 mL of 37°C PBS and place the holder with acoustic membrane on the bottom of the dish.
Cut into the vitelline membrane around the entire CAM while the egg content is in the weighing boat.
Hold the edge of the vitelline membrane to prevent cutting into the CAM.
Use a tablespoon to scoop up the cut-out membrane containing the embryo and CAM from the weighing boat.
Visually inspect whether the cut-out membrane containing the embryo and CAM is still attached to the remainder yolk sack membrane.
Make an extra cut with scissors if necessary to detach the membrane.
Tilt the spoon slightly to remove excess yolk without drying out the membrane.
Transfer the cut-out membrane containing the embryo and CAM to a 1 L Petri dish submerged in 37 °C PBS.
Remove the tablespoon from the Petri dish.
Use small tweezers to grab one edge of the membrane.
Gently swirl around the membrane to remove remaining yolk.
Move the membrane containing the embryo and CAM above the holder with acoustic membrane using the tweezers.
Pin down one corner of the membrane containing the embryo and CAM in one corner with an insect specimen pin, avoiding vessels in the CAM.
Pin down the diagonally opposite corner of the membrane containing the embryo and CAM with a second insect specimen pin.
Lift the holder with the acoustic membrane containing the embryo and CAM from the 37 °C PBS slowly.
Tilt the holder slightly to remove most of the PBS.
Use small tweezers to stretch and evenly distribute the membrane containing the embryo and CAM over the holder with acoustic membrane.
Pin down the rest of the membrane containing the embryo and CAM.
Place the holder with acoustic membrane into a microscopy setup kept at 37 °C.
Place a coverslip or an acoustically and optically transparent membrane on top of the region of interest on the embryo or CAM for optical visualization.
Submerge the preferred ultrasound transducer in a 37 °C water bath.
Position the ultrasound transducer in the desired spot with the required standoff distance.
Place the weighing boat in the water bath with the transparent wall facing the transducer.
Ensure the weighing boat is level with the transducer without allowing water to enter.
Add a microscope or laser setup on top of the embryo or CAM vessels if desired.
Fill a 2 L beaker glass with 37 °C PBS.
Place an upside-down 500 mL beaker in the bottom of the 2 L beaker to raise the weighing boat closer to the PBS surface.
Avoid introducing air inside the inverted 500 mL beaker.
Submerge the setup containing the egg content in a 37 °C water bath.
Remove the egg content as described in sections 1.2, 1.3, or 1.4.
Wet the egg content with 37 °C PBS to prevent it from sticking excessively.
Cover the embryo with clear cling film to maintain its position and prevent movement.
Place the weighing boat containing the egg content in a 90 mm diameter Petri dish.
Submerge the Petri dish slowly into the PBS.
Take out the egg content as described in section 1.2, 1.3, or 1.4.
Prepare a 2% agarose solution in demi water by heating it up to between 80-95 °C.
Cool the glass beaker with the dissolved agarose solution under running cold water.
Pour the cooled agarose solution into a flat container to create an about 1 mm thick agarose pad.
Cut the cooled and set agarose pad to the desired size using a scalpel.
Place the agarose pad on top of the embryo and CAM.
Add a few drops (~30 µL) of 37 °C PBS onto the top of the agarose pad.
Position the desired ultrasound transducer.
